title: Interval boundary tests for the Joyal fibrations
statement:
Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, inner horns, degreewise products and functor simplicial sets as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the Joyal model structure of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Put $\partial\Delta^n$ equal to the union of the proper faces of $\Delta^n$, with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. Define a finite simplicial set $J$ by starting with an edge $a:0\to1$, freely adjoining two edges $b,c:1\to0$, and freely adjoining a $2$-simplex with successive edges $(a,b)$ and long edge $\mathrm{id}_0$, and a $2$-simplex with successive edges $(c,a)$ and long edge $\mathrm{id}_1$. Freely adjoining means taking degreewise simplicial pushouts of boundary inclusions; the stated degenerate edges and all vertices are identified as specified, with no further relations on simplices.

Call a map Kan anodyne if it belongs to the smallest class containing all horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$, and all isomorphisms, and closed under pushouts, retracts and transfinite composition (using colimits at limit ordinals). Both endpoint inclusions $\{\varepsilon\}\hookrightarrow J$, $\varepsilon=0,1$, are Kan anodyne. For every $n\geq0$ and $\varepsilon=0,1$, the inclusion
$$s_{\varepsilon,n}:(\partial\Delta^n\times J)\cup(\Delta^n\times\{\varepsilon\})\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\times J$$
is a trivial cofibration in the Joyal model structure; the union is the degreewise union of these simplicial subsets. For any map $p:X\to Y$ between quasicategories in one universe, $p$ is a Joyal fibration if and only if it has the right lifting property against every inner horn inclusion and every $s_{\varepsilon,n}$.

source.place: Cisinski, construction 3.3.1, Proposition 3.3.2 and Definition 3.3.3 (printed pp.92-94) for J and its endpoint Kan anodyneness; Remark 3.3.4 and Definition 3.3.7 (pp.94-95), and Theorem 2.4.19 (p.57) for the boundary-cylinder generators and the fibration test between fibrant objects. The already-supplied quasicategory/fibrancy identification is in lem-coef-joyal-model-structure; Theorem 3.6.8 identifies Cisinski's weak-equivalence convention with its hFun convention. Revision July 30, 2026, read directly in the online PDF and a private sandbox text extraction on 2026-10-17. No Stacks tag states this result. WANTED: archived source in literature/.

from.place: Proof paragraph 2, displayed derived R Hom / R lim calculation: coherent diagram realization through finite-Reedy localization, at the source-attachment join/cone comparison. Legitimate ordinary pullback of the cone comparison over a varying joint endpoint base. Identification of Joyal fibrations and weak equivalences between quasicategories, used to factor the graph of the comparison. At this identification, interval boundary tests replace an uncited appeal to the fibration clause; they do not identify equivalence-edge lifting by themselves.
